subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw support user-authored per-skill preferences as a markdown sidecar, a structured config-only mechanism, or leave this to skill/package authors for now?
rationale: The implementation shape changes public skill-loading semantics and prompt authority, and repository policy requires maintainer intent before adding new config or context-loading surfaces.

options.title: Adopt a markdown sidecar
options.body: Standardize a user-authored `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar with lower authority than `SKILL.md`, include it in version/watch invalidation, and document the security boundary.

options.title: Use structured config only
options.body: Keep natural-language preferences out of automatic prompt loading and document `skills.entries.<key>.config` as the supported per-skill customization path when skill code can consume it.

options.title: Defer to package authors
options.body: Do not add core loading behavior yet; ask skill authors to document optional companion files inside their own `SKILL.md` until broader skill composition decisions settle.

recommendation.title: Adopt a markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Standardize a user-authored `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar with lower authority than `SKILL.md`, include it in version/watch invalidation, and document the security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current local source history for the skill loader and skill docs points to this person as the best available area-routing candidate.
